title: Forming and Defending Judgements: Capstone Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together in a case study in which participants investigate an ambiguous issue, form and document a judgement, write it up for a committee and defend it under challenge.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together in a case study in which participants investigate an ambiguous issue, form and document a judgement, write it up for a committee and defend it under challenge.
Learning Objectives: Combine evidence, questioning, judgement and writing skills in a realistic scenario
Document reasoning so that it is defensible under later scrutiny
Defend a judgement before a mock committee and set personal development priorities
Syllabus: Case briefing, analysis and a fact-finding interview
Recording the rationale: options considered and reasons for the decision
Drafting a short committee paper and escalation note
Workshop: presenting, defending and reflecting on the judgement
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and financial crime analysts, officers and advisers in their first years in the role
Experienced control function staff moving into advisory, investigation or reporting roles who want to sharpen their judgement and writing
Business-side risk and control staff, such as first-line risk teams, who advise colleagues and escalate concerns
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of working in or alongside a compliance, risk or financial crime function is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein, Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment (2021)
Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
